subject: physics_2
question_text: Obtain Gauss's law for magnetism and explain it.

verification.note: The 1+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero — Δφ = B·ΔS cos θ per element, φ = Σ B·ΔS = 0 summed over the closed surface — because isolated magnetic poles (monopoles) do not exist; the electric contrast is φ = Σ E·ΔS = q/ε₀, nonzero when charge is enclosed. The figure (closed surface, area element ΔS, outward normal n, field B at angle θ) is drawn without diagram marks because the question does not ask for a diagram.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Statement
steps.mark_note: Net flux zero, any closed surface
lines: Gauss's law for magnetism: the net
magnetic flux through any closed surface
is zero. The number of field lines leaving
the surface equals the number entering it.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two words carry it: net and closed — the law says nothing about open surfaces.
steps.why: The statement is the law itself, so it opens the answer. Net and closed are the load-bearing words: through an open surface the magnetic flux need not be zero at all.
common_mistakes: Dropping the word closed. Flux through an open surface (one turn of a coil) is not zero — that flux drives induction in the next chapter.
Saying the flux is small. The law says exactly zero, always.

recall.must_convey: That the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero.
accept: net magnetic flux through a closed surface is zero
as many lines leave as enter
reject: flux is q by epsilon nought

steps.memory_tip: Closed surface, net flux, zero — the three words that are the law.

steps.label: The closed surface
steps.margin_note: No diagram mark is asked, but the figure fixes S, ΔS, n and θ for the working below it.
steps.why: The figure names everything the derivation uses: a closed surface S sitting in a field B, one small area element ΔS on it, the outward normal n, and the angle θ between n and B.
common_mistakes: Drawing an open surface such as a flat disc. The law is about a CLOSED surface — draw a surface that encloses a volume.

recall.must_convey: That a closed surface is drawn in a magnetic field with one area element ΔS marked, its outward normal n at angle θ to B.
accept: draw the closed surface in the field
mark an area element with its normal
show theta between the normal and B

steps.memory_tip: Draw the surface first, then one small patch on it — the whole law is that patch, summed.

steps.label: Flux through an element
lines: Divide the closed surface S into many
small area elements. Take one element of
area ΔS, with outward normal n at angle θ
to the field B at that place.
The magnetic flux through this element is
steps.margin_note: One patch at a time: only the part of B along the normal sends flux through the patch, hence cos θ.
steps.why: Flux counts field lines crossing the patch, and only the component of B along the normal crosses it — that is what cos θ selects. The whole law is this one patch, summed.
common_mistakes: Writing sin θ. Flux uses the component of B along the normal, so cos θ.
Measuring θ from the surface instead of from the normal.

recall.must_convey: That the surface is divided into small elements and the flux through one element is B times ΔS times cos θ.
accept: divide the surface into small elements
flux is B delta S cos theta
component of B along the normal

steps.memory_tip: Flux through a patch = field × area × cos θ, with θ taken from the normal.

steps.label: Net flux is zero
lines: Add the flux from every element of the
closed surface. As many field lines enter
the surface as leave it, so the sum is
zero:
This holds for every closed surface,
whatever its shape or size.
steps.margin_note: The sum runs over ALL the area elements of the closed surface — that is what Σ stands for.
steps.why: Field lines close into loops, so any line that enters the closed surface must come out again. Entering flux is negative, leaving flux positive, and over the whole surface they cancel exactly.
common_mistakes: Claiming the flux through each element is zero. Individual elements carry flux — only the SUM over the closed surface vanishes.
Restricting the result to special surfaces. It holds for any closed surface, of any shape.

recall.must_convey: That summing B·ΔS over all elements of the closed surface gives zero, for any closed surface.
accept: sum of B delta S is zero

steps.memory_tip: Every line that goes in must come out — the sum cancels to zero.

steps.label: Contrast with electrostatics
lines: In electrostatics the flux through a
closed surface is q/ε₀, not zero, because
isolated charges exist:
Isolated magnetic poles (monopoles) do
not exist. The simplest magnetic unit is
a dipole, so the flux in and the flux out
always cancel:

lines.text: Net magnetic flux: φ = Σ B·ΔS = 0

steps.margin_note: The explain part of the question lives here: the zero says magnetic monopoles do not exist.
steps.why: The two Gauss laws differ in exactly one physical fact: charge can be enclosed alone, a magnetic pole cannot. That is why one flux is q/ε₀ and the other is always zero.
common_mistakes: Writing the magnetic flux as m/μ₀ by copying the electric form. There is no enclosed pole strength — the flux is zero.
Ending without saying WHY it is zero. The examiner reads for the words monopoles do not exist.

recall.must_convey: That the electric flux is q/ε₀ because isolated charges exist, while the magnetic flux is zero because monopoles do not.
accept: electric flux is q by epsilon nought
the basic magnetic unit is a dipole

steps.memory_tip: Charges can sit alone, poles cannot — so one flux is q/ε₀ and the other is zero.

insider_note: Obtain and explain are two halves: the sum reaching zero is the obtain, and the sentence monopoles do not exist is the explain — answers that stop at the equation lose the last mark.
